extraction.name: HELVIPAD
extraction.description: A real-world dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation, featuring 40K video frames from video sequences across diverse environments, including crowded indoor and outdoor scenes with various lighting conditions. Collected using two 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup and a LiDAR sensor, the dataset includes accurate depth and disparity labels by projecting 3D point clouds onto equirectangular images.
extraction.creator: Mehdi Zayene, Jannik Endres, Albias Havolli, Charles Corbière, Salim Cherkaoui, Alexandre Kontouli, Alexandre Alahi
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data were collected using a custom-built rig equipped with two omnidirectional cameras in a vertical arrangement, which prevents occlusion, and paired with a synchronized LiDAR sensor to provide high-quality depth measurements. The dataset consists of 29 video sequences (26 video sequences mentioned in supplementary material) captured in dynamic indoor and outdoor scenes across a university campus under diverse weather and lighting conditions, recorded at a frame rate of 10 Hz.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Missing depth values were handled through depth completion techniques to increase label density for an augmented training set. The depth completion process interpolates missing values and removes out-of-distribution samples.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of synchronized omnidirectional stereo images from two vertically-arranged cameras and LiDAR point clouds. Images were originally captured at 1024 pixels width and subsequently cropped and downsized to 512 pixels width. LiDAR point clouds were projected onto equirectangular images to obtain depth maps and subsequently disparity maps.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Depth and disparity labels were created by projecting LiDAR point clouds onto equirectangular images using an optimized transformation. The process involved: (1) selecting key 3D points from LiDAR scans on a chessboard and their corresponding image pixels, (2) applying initial rotation/translation transformations, (3) converting to spherical coordinates, (4) optimizing rotation and translation parameters by minimizing projection error using BFGS optimization. An augmented training set was created using automated depth completion with temporal aggregation, interpolation, and filtering.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Alignment accuracy was assessed by calculating pixel error between 200 randomly selected LiDAR points and their image positions, resulting in an average error of 1.7 pixels. For visually challenging areas (e.g., object edges), the error was 8.0 pixels. The depth completion pipeline was validated by splitting LiDAR point clouds into training and test sets and computing depth estimation metrics on the test set, maintaining very low error rates while increasing labeled pixel ratio from 12% to 61%.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: One depth/disparity label per pixel (where available). Original labels cover 12% of pixels; augmented labels cover 61% of pixels.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: LiDAR sensor (Ouster OS1-64) for depth measurement, BFGS optimization algorithm for LiDAR-to-image mapping, automated depth completion pipeline with temporal aggregation, k-nearest neighbor interpolation, and uncertainty-based filtering.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is collected from a university campus environment, which may limit generalization to other settings. Indoor-trained models show clear limitations in generalizing to outdoor scenes, particularly at night. The dataset captures specific geographic and demographic contexts that may not represent all real-world scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The depth completion approach is limited for fast-moving objects like cars due to the temporal aggregation window. LiDAR point clouds are sparse compared to high-resolution camera images, with ground-truth depth labels covering only a fraction of total pixels (12% before completion, 61% after). Occlusions were not explicitly handled in the LiDAR-camera calibration, though the small baseline minimizes their impact. The dataset is limited to university campus environments.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to help mobile robots navigate and interact in dynamic human environments, with applications in autonomous driving, healthcare, and agriculture. It captures human pedestrian activity across indoor and outdoor settings, which could improve robot safety and navigation in human-populated spaces.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset captures human pedestrians in various indoor and outdoor environments on a university campus. Images include people in corridors, halls, squares, parking areas, and footpaths under different lighting conditions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training, validation, and testing of omnidirectional stereo depth estimation models. It serves as a benchmark for developing models capable of navigating in human environments. The dataset is split into train-val (29,407 frames from 20 sequences) and test (10,146 frames from 6 sequences) sets. An augmented training set with increased label density via depth completion is provided for improved model training.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Depth completion pipeline using temporal aggregation of LiDAR point clouds, k-nearest neighbor weighted interpolation on spherical grid points, and filtering based on uncertainty and out-of-distribution thresholds to fill missing depth values
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Augmented training set created through depth completion to increase label density from 12% to 61%; photometric data augmentation applied during training to handle variability in lighting conditions; circular padding applied during inference for 360° continuity
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Projection of LiDAR point clouds onto equirectangular images through coordinate transformation and optimization; cropping of unnecessary regions (sky, ground); calibration using chessboard-based point selection and BFGS optimization to align LiDAR and camera coordinates; conversion to spherical coordinates and equirectangular projection
